spans.s: bhittī-phalaka, m., lit. wall-board, a sitting-bench or stool against a wall, for an infant of six months to be placed on: (paryaṅkaḥ … tad yathāpi nāma) ṣaṇmāsajātasya dārakasya ˚kaḥ (no v.l. in mss.) LV 〔63.7〕 (prose).

bhit(t)vara, adj., ruined, broken-down: (of a house,) read bhitvara (with ms. Ḱ) or ˚ru (with 3 mss., KN) in SP 〔85.4〕 (vs), for durbalam of both edd., which the preceding and parallel sudurbalaṃ makes improbable; Tib. ḥjig (ñe) supports a form of bhid-; read for the next word bhairavaṃ, with all Nep. mss. of KN, also Ḱ, and Tib. ḥjigs, for KNʼs em. itvara; this word (q.v.) is inappropriate here, yet similar enough in mg. to have helped in the creation of bhit(t)vara, as if bhid- plus tvara, modelled on i-tvara and Skt. ga-tvara; the latter has a mg. virtually identical with that required here. Is this the word intended by vidvarena (vi = bhi repeatedly here) in Dutreuil, C fragm. 〔XIIIvo〕, for which Pali SN 〔i.131.11〕 has bhindanena, v.l. ˚rena? See Barua and Mitra 〔211, 213〕.
